topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview of cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's learning outcomes, relates them to previous material on tumorigenesis, and outlines the hallmarks of cancer framework.

topics.label: Sustaining proliferative signaling and evading growth suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the signaling cascades and mutations—such as Wnt/APC, receptor tyrosine kinases, and TGF-beta—that drive uncontrolled cell proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation block in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how malignancies in hematological lineages and intestinal crypts prevent cells from executing terminal differentiation while maintaining proliferative states.

topics.label: Resisting cell death through apoptotic deregulation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how cancer cells circumvent programmed cell death through mutations in p53 and imbalances in pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins such as Bax and BCL2.

topics.label: Enabling replicative immortality and senescence mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells bypass the Hayflick limit via telomerase reactivation alongside the stress-response pathways that normally enforce cellular senescence.

topics.label: Deregulating cellular metabolism
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the metabolic reprogramming of cancer cells toward aerobic glycolysis (the Warburg effect) and the epigenetic consequences of oncometabolite accumulation.

topics.label: Inducing angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the angiogenic switch, explaining how tumors overcome hypoxia and nutrient limits by shifting the balance between pro- and anti-angiogenic factors.

topics.label: Activating invasion and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the metastatic cascade, seed-and-soil microenvironmental dynamics, and the clonal genomic features that enable distant tumor dissemination.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and summary
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by synthesising the hallmarks, referencing further reading, and closing with logistical housekeeping.
